subject: CobaltPay: sudden throughput drop on reserved pool — escalation
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom@cobaltpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, CobaltPay SRE <sre@cobaltpay.com>
Date: 2027-05-27T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: sudden token-queueing and 5xx surge on our reserved pool

Hi Kimberly —

Heads up: starting ~15:30 PDT we see a large uptick in tail latency and 5xx errors from the model route we've pinned to our reserved GPU pool. Throughput (tokens/s) has dropped ~40% compared to the baseline and request timeouts are ticking up. This is affecting our fraud-detector pipeline — we have alerts firing and customers are seeing degraded UX.

We attached the error logs and a short sample of request IDs in the zip. Can you confirm whether there was any maintenance or config change on your side? We purchased the reserved tier explicitly for predictable throughput; this is a hard break for us during peak.

Urgent ask: immediate mitigation and ETA for capacity recovery.

—Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Infrastructure, CobaltPay
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom@cobaltpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden token-queueing and 5xx surge on our reserved pool

Tom —

Thanks for the quick flag and for sending logs. No scheduled maintenance on our side. I’m escalating to infra immediately and have looped David (on-call infra lead) to triage.

Immediate plan:
- David will validate whether the reserved pool has reached GPU utilization headroom and check eviction/fallback rules.
- If we confirm saturation, we’ll trigger an emergency burst (if allowed) and roll traffic to a compatible fallback model variant while we stabilize.
- I’ll coordinate a short sync once we have root-cause signals — target within 30 minutes.

I’ve attached the logs you sent to our incident ticket. Please stand by; we know this impacts your live customers and will treat it as priority.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: CobaltPay production degradation — exec attention requested

Folks — forwarding an urgent customer escalation (CobaltPay). Reserved capacity route is showing sustained throughput loss and higher 5xx tail. Customer purchased a dedicated reservation for predictable throughput; they're in production peak.

High-level asks:
- Marissa: need authorization to offer immediate burst credits or a temporary overage charge to cover the emergency capacity while we remediate. What level of credit can we promise without legal approval?
- Sofia: please join the customer bridge if available and help coordinate communications; we need to be explicit about ETA and fallback behavior.
- David: triage and advise whether this is a software/kernel regression or a traffic pattern (cache miss) problem — your initial read is critical.

I will run the bridge and own customer comms. Customer is requesting an ETA within 30 minutes.

—Kim
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T16:52:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CobaltPay production degradation — infra triage notes

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed: the reserved GPU pool servicing CobaltPay shows GPU utilization hitting sustained 98% across the hot shard group. Token processing latency distribution shifted — p95 doubled, p99 tripled.
- Error pattern: a rise in OOM/retry windows at the runtime layer correlated with a sudden increase in KV cache miss rate for a small set of prompts (hot keys). That causes increased recomputation and CPU/GPU stalls.
- No kernel upgrade or deploy in the timeframe. No autoscaler triggers fired because the reservation blocks autoscaling beyond the quota unless explicit burst is authorized.

Immediate remediation steps we executed (ongoing):
1) Throttle/queue lower-priority routes for CobaltPay within the same reservation to free headroom for the critical route.
2) Apply a temporary model-variant fallback (lower-quantization) for a small percentage of traffic to reduce memory pressure.
3) Recommend emergency burst (one-off) to provision extra capacity while we redistribute hot keys into a cached prefix group.

Estimated time-to-stable: 45–90 minutes assuming burst authorization now. Without burst, remediation via throttling+fallback will reduce customer impact but may not fully restore nominal throughput during peak.

Attaching metrics snapshot: sla-metrics-snapshot.csv (includes GPU headroom, KV-cache hit rates, and request ID samples).

—David
David Kim
Director, Serving Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom@cobaltpay.com>, Elena Morales <elena@cobaltpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: CobaltPay incident update and next steps (reserved pool saturation)

Tom / Elena —

Short update and plan after infra triage:
- Cause: sudden, high-volume skew to a small set of prompts that produced KV-cache churn on your reserved pool. That churn caused memory pressure and increased recomputation; GPUs reached headroom limits.
- Immediate mitigations we applied: throttled non-critical routes within your reservation, rolled ~12% of traffic to a lower-memory model variant, and tuned runtime retry windows. These reduced the error rate and brought latency down from p99 spike back toward baseline for most traffic.
- To fully restore nominal throughput during your peak window we recommend an emergency burst (+2 GPU nodes for 3 hours). David confirmed this will allow us to rehydrate the KV-prefix cache and rebalance hot keys.

Request: can you confirm approval for emergency burst authorization? We can provision within ~12 minutes of approval and will continue to monitor with you in a short bridge. If you prefer not to accept temporary burst charges, we will keep the throttles/fallbacks in place and follow up with a deeper root-cause remediation plan (hot-key partitioning + longer-term cache-pin).

Next steps:
- If approved, we’ll provision capacity and run an immediate rebalancing job; expected full recovery within 45 minutes of provisioning.
- We will follow up with a post-incident summary and recommended config guardrails to avoid recurrence (KV pinning, request sampling to detect hot prompts).

Apologies for the disruption — we will treat this as a priority and stay on the bridge until you confirm stable behavior.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference
